items.shortLine: Meet Neta & walk through your plan
items.detailText: Meet Neta on Day 1. You'll walk through your onboarding plan together - what to expect these first few weeks, and how the two of you will work together.
A walk around the Tel Aviv office with Tal, one of your teammates - where things are and how the space works, from someone who isn't your manager.
A self-paced session on Veridian's vision, values, departments, and the three offices - Tel Aviv, London, and Austin. First of six sessions on the company.
A short self-paced course on the security basics everyone at Veridian needs to know. Due by Day 7.
A quick read on how people work together at Veridian and what's expected of everyone. Due by Day 7.
Email, calendar, and shared drive, set up before you even start so it's waiting for you on Day 1.
Slack access lands Day 1. It's where the People Partners team and the managers you support communicate day to day.
Notion access is ready Day 1, home for Veridian's People policies, playbooks, and internal HR documentation.
HiBob is ready Day 1, the HRIS you'll work in daily on behalf of the managers you support, plus your own employee profile and time off.
No buddy assigned yet. Your manager will pair you with one soon - they're your go-to for the everyday questions.
Neta walks you through the full operating picture of the People function in one sitting: mission, metrics, workflows, key interfaces, and where to find docs and reports.
Connect with a fellow HRBP on the team to compare notes on what supporting your own set of managers looks like day to day.
Connect with the team's senior HRBP, a good resource once you're navigating trickier situations with the managers you support.
Get set up on benefits and logistics, with a direct contact at HR from here on.
A self-paced look at what Veridian builds: Knowledge Hub, AI Assistant, AI Agents, and Governance. Session 2 of 6 on the company.
A short course on data privacy fundamentals, required for everyone at Veridian. Due by Day 14.
A self-paced session on Veridian's market and the kinds of customers it serves. Session 3 of 6 on the company.
A self-paced session on Veridian's business model. Session 4 of 6 on the company.
A self-paced session on the key metrics Veridian tracks. Session 5 of 6 on the company.
Sit in with Tal Harari on a real conversation with one of the managers she supports. It's the fastest way to see what a strong advisory conversation actually sounds like.
Emma is one of the senior leaders you support as part of the Executive team - a first conversation on how that partnership plays out on the Product side.
Stay aligned with Neta this week and flag anything that already feels off track.
A self-paced session on Veridian's strategic direction and near-term roadmap, the last of the six company sessions.
Finance's director, and one of the teams you'll be supporting. A first sense of how his team runs day to day.

items.shortLine: Say hello to Yael, your skip-level
items.detailText: Meet Yael Shalev, VP People, the leader of the whole People function you're now part of.
A quick sync with Neta this week to catch anything before it piles up.
A session with Neta on where People fits into Veridian and what it's aiming for this year.
A self-guided read through the policies that matter most day to day: hybrid work, security, and expenses.
This week's check-in doubles as your 30-day review. Step back with Neta to see how the first month matched the plan and re-prioritize together.
A working conversation with Maya on how People supports the executive team's people needs, and where you fit into that.
Michael is one of the senior leaders you support as part of the Executive team - a first conversation on what that partnership looks like from the Revenue side.
Ben manages IT, one of the teams you'll be supporting. A first sense of his day-to-day priorities.
Finance, one of the teams you'll be supporting, is run by Michal. A first sense of how her team works.
Keep the weekly rhythm going with Neta and raise anything that needs attention.
Nathan manages Legal, one of the teams you'll be supporting. A first sense of what he'll come to you for.
Business Operations, one of the teams you'll be supporting, is led by Hannah. A first sense of her priorities.
A short sync with Neta to stay in step and catch anything early.
Your weekly touchpoint with Neta. Stay aligned and clear out any blockers.

internalGaps: The office tour used a fallback guide (Tal Harari, a Tel Aviv teammate) - see the pending Human Buddy assignment already reflected in week 1's plan, this is not a separate gap.

hrbp_email is not set for this employee, so no 'meeting with your HRBP' item exists in this plan. Plausibly intentional since she's part of the HRBP function herself, but that's not confirmed in the data - flagged rather than assumed.

The Teams catalog has no entry for 'People Partners' - team mission and core_tools are unknown. The team-member intros (Rachel Cooper, Tal Harari) and the department overview used real employee-table records and department.mission/primary_kpis directly instead.
company_overview only has basic summary fields (name, category, employee count, offices) - no product description, ICP, or business-model detail exists anywhere in the source data.
DEMO ASSUMPTION (see prompts/process-expert.md and README.md): business-track LMS sessions 3-6 have no real source data behind them - descriptions are topical only.
No manager intake was supplied for this run, so professionalMentor is null - no mentor item was written, and this is a pipeline limitation for this test run, not a fact about the employee.

Yael Shalev has hrbp_email pointing to this employee but is also her skip_manager_email - an organizational contradiction in the source data (an HRBP formally 'supporting' someone above them in their own reporting line). Excluded from peopleSupported by a code-level filter in lib/context.js; her existing skip-level relationship (week 4) is unaffected.

Her 8 supported managers are scheduled as 8 separate individual 1:1s across weeks 3-6, not a group session - the CEO, CPO and CRO are never bundled into a shared session with each other or with the Finance/IT/Legal/Ops managers she supports.

The 'Shadow a real advisory conversation' item (week 3) names Tal Harari as facilitator - she's the team's senior HRBP and the natural real candidate, but the manager should confirm this assignment explicitly before the plan ships, since the underlying plan item itself didn't name a specific person.
This plan does not include applied 'doing' work tickets (out of scope by design for this pipeline).
